subject: Caspian sea disappears on world map plot

messages.author: 140af76444204638
messages.subject: Caspian sea disappears on world map plot
parts:
Hello,

I'm using this shape file from Natural Earth data to plot a world map with ggplot2, but for some reason the caspian sea is missing on the plot. It's there if I use plot(), but not in my ggplot.

Here's my code:

library(maptools)
library(ggplot2)

world.sp <- readShapePoly("50m-land/50m_land", proj4string=CRS("+proj=longlat +ellps=WGS84 +datum=WGS84 +no_defs"))
world.sp <- fortify(world.sp)

ggplot(world.sp, aes(long, lat, group=group)) + geom_polygon()

Anyone know how to solve this problem? 

Best,
Kristoffer

messages.subject: Re: Caspian sea disappears on world map plot
parts:
Hi,

I figured out that my problem was caused by how ggplot handles holes in polygons, as Winston mentioned. I wasn't aware that ggplot plots holes as a separate polygon above the land polygon (in this case) and not as a true hole, I can get the caspian sea to show up if I set "fill = hole". However, It's not an ideal solutions as I want all water area to be transparent. 

Thanks!
Kristoffer
